correctness.rationale: The established support-vertex inequality gives the basic gap bound. The odd equality case follows from forced support vertices, parity of paired domination, and the fact that adjacent supports would create a smaller paired set. For even order, the saturated support case is exactly a corona; pairing through a maximum matching of its core gives the exact formula for paired domination, and equality forces a star core. In the one-fewer-support case, parity and the forced-support argument imply an independent support set and a universal extra total-dominating vertex, which yields the second extremal family. These arguments cover all orders and the stated small exceptions.
